sanskrit: asmāñ juṣadhvam asavo 'dya mā naḥ purā jaraso 'savo vadhiṣṭa | pākā gṛṇīmas tava vīryāya śataṃ himān adhipatir na ehi ||
english: Attend upon us, O vital breaths, today; let not the vital breaths strike us down before old age. Humbly we hymn thee for thy might — come to us as overlord for a hundred winters.

sanskrit: un mṛṇo agād ārjunam agāt suśrud bhagavo gopāya mā | ahne 'dyātmānaṃ pari dade sūryaprāṇo bhavāmi ||
english: The white (breath) has gone forth upward; the bright one has gone forth — hear well, O Bhaga, protect me. Today I deliver my self over to the day; may I become one whose vital breath is the sun.

sanskrit: ni mṛṇo agād āsitam agāt suśrud bhagavo gopāya mā | rātraye 'dyātmānaṃ pari dade agniprāṇo bhavāmi ||
english: The dark (breath) has gone down; the black one has gone forth — hear well, O Bhaga, protect me. Today I deliver my self over to the night; may I become one whose vital breath is Agni.

sanskrit: anābhūr asy anābho 'nābhuvo bhūyāsma | sa yatra tvaṃ prajāpate trir ekasyāhnaḥ prajāḥ saṃpaśyasi | tatra mām api saṃ paśya- -anaṣṭapaśur bhuvanasya gopāḥ ||
english: Thou art one who has not been harmed; unharmed, may we be unharmed. There where thou, O Prajāpati, dost behold thy creatures three times in a single day — there do thou look upon me as well, O guardian of the world, one whose cattle have not been lost.

sanskrit: yathā mṛgaṃ ropayasi tiraś carmātividhyasi | evā tvam ugra oṣadhe amuṃ ropaya mām abhi ||
english: As thou causest the deer to be fixed (with longing) and piercest through its hide, so, O potent herb, do thou fix yonder one (with longing) toward me.

sanskrit: bandhaś cemā upadhiś ca madhuman nau samañjanam | dvārau bhagasyemā ūrū mṛgas tṛṣyann ivā cara ||
english: A bond and a snare too — sweet is the ointment for the two of us. These two thighs are the twin doors of Bhaga; come (to me) like a deer thirsting (for water).

sanskrit: abhi tvādhām abhidhinā jāleneva mahājaṣam | yathā mama kratāv aso mama citte sacāvahai ||
english: With a snare I have bound thee about, as (one binds) a great fish with a net, so that thou mayest be in my will, and we two may dwell together in my heart.

sanskrit: ahaṃ vai tvad uttarāsmy adha tvam upadhir mama | saṃ nau badhnāmi saṃbandhanena yathāsāvāvicartyāv ā mṛtyor ā parāvataḥ ||
english: I am indeed the superior one over thee; thou art then my foothold. I bind the two of us together with a binding-spell, so that we two may roam about (inseparably) from here to the distance of death.

sanskrit: apocchantī duṣvapnyam apa durhārdam ucchatam | apoṣṭaṃ sarvaṃ kṣetriyaṃ sarvāś ca yātudhānyaḥ ||
english: Driving away ill-dreaming, driving out malevolence, as (the stars) rise — drive away all hereditary disease (kṣetriya) and all the she-demons (yātudhānī).

sanskrit: ud agātāṃ bhagavatī vicṛtau nāma tārake | vi kṣetriyasya muñcatāṃ saṃgranthiṃ hṛdayasya ca ||
english: The two auspicious stars named Vicṛtau have risen; may they loosen asunder the knot of hereditary disease and the knot of the heart as well.

sanskrit: namo astu varatrābhyo nama īṣāyugebhyaḥ | mṛgāyāraṇye tiṣṭhate kṣetriyāyākaraṃ namaḥ ||
english: Homage be to the thongs, homage to the shaft-yoke. To the hereditary disease that stands as a wild deer in the forest I have paid homage.

sanskrit: ākhor idaṃ kṣaitrapatyaṃ manoś ca mānavasya ca | manaḥ sarvasya paśyata iha bhūyaḥ syād iti ||
english: This hereditary affliction of the field belongs to the mole, and to Manu, and to the human. May the mind of every beholder say: 'Let it be here abundantly.'
